questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Why is a four-level laser (such as Nd:YAG) much easier to bring to threshold than a three-level laser (such as Ruby)?
optionsEn: Because it does not need an optical cavity
Because its lower lasing level is an excited state that is virtually empty at thermal equilibrium, requiring minimal pumping for population inversion
Because its upper level has zero lifetime
Because it emits only spontaneous radiation
questions.explanationEn: In a 3-level laser, more than half of all ground-state atoms must be pumped to invert $N_1 > N_0$; in a 4-level laser, the lower lasing level empties rapidly to the ground state, so almost any population in the upper level achieves inversion.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: The Paschen-Back effect occurs when the external magnetic field $B$ is:
optionsEn: Much weaker than the internal spin-orbit coupling field
Much stronger than the internal spin-orbit coupling, decoupling $\mathbf{L}$ and $\mathbf{S}$
questions.explanationEn: In the strong-field Paschen-Back regime, Zeeman interaction dominates spin-orbit coupling, so $\mathbf{L}$ and $\mathbf{S}$ precess independently around $\mathbf{B}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: The Franck-Condon principle for electronic transitions in diatomic molecules states that:
optionsEn: Vibrational quantum number must satisfy $\Delta v = \pm 1$ only
Electronic transitions occur so rapidly that the internuclear separation $R$ remains essentially unchanged (vertical transitions on a potential energy diagram)
questions.explanationEn: Because electrons are thousands of times lighter than nuclei, electronic transitions happen instantaneously relative to nuclear motion, favoring vertical transitions with largest vibrational wavefunction overlap.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which coupling scheme becomes dominant in heavy multi-electron atoms (large $Z$) where spin-orbit interaction is stronger than residual electron-electron electrostatic repulsion?
questions.explanationEn: Because spin-orbit coupling scales as $Z^4$, in heavy atoms each electron's $\mathbf{l}_i$ and $\mathbf{s}_i$ couple first into $\mathbf{j}_i$, and then $\mathbf{J} = \sum \mathbf{j}_i$ ($jj$ coupling).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In the rovibrational infrared spectrum of a diatomic molecule (like HCl), the P-branch and R-branch correspond respectively to:
questions.explanationEn: For $\Delta v = +1$, transitions with $J' - J'' = -1$ form the lower-frequency P-branch, and $J' - J'' = +1$ form the higher-frequency R-branch (with $\Delta J = 0$ Q-branch forbidden for $^1\Sigma$ states).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: For an atomic level with given $L, S, J$, which of the following statements about the Landé $g$-factor $g_J = 1 + \frac{J(J+1) + S(S+1) - L(L+1)}{2J(J+1)}$ are TRUE?
optionsEn: For every atomic state, $g_J$ must lie between 1 and 2
For any pure singlet state ($S = 0, J = L$), $g_J = 1$

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: For a $^1 D_2$ state, what is the value of the Landé $g$-factor?
questions.explanationEn: Since $S = 0$ (singlet), $J = L$, so $g_J = 1$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the Landé $g$-factor for the $^2 P_{3/2}$ state? (Round to 2 decimal places.)

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A continuous-wave laser outputs $10\text{ mW}$ at wavelength $\lambda = 600\text{ nm}$. Taking $hc = 2 \times 10^{-25}\text{ J}\cdot\text{m}$, how many photons are emitted per second, in units of $10^{16}\text{ s}^{-1}$?
questions.explanationEn: Energy per photon $E = hc/\lambda = \frac{2 \times 10^{-25}}{6 \times 10^{-7}} = \frac{1}{3} \times 10^{-18}\text{ J}$. Rate = $\frac{10^{-2}}{\frac{1}{3} \times 10^{-18}} = 3 \times 10^{16}\text{ photons/s}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A diatomic molecule has vibrational constant $\bar{\nu}_e = 2000\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (harmonic approximation). What is its zero-point vibrational energy in $\text{cm}^{-1}$?
questions.explanationEn: Zero-point energy $E_0 = \frac{1}{2}\bar{\nu}_e = 1000\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In a diatomic molecule, centrifugal distortion modifies the rotational energy levels from $B J(J+1)$ to:
questions.explanationEn: Rapid rotation stretches the bond slightly, increasing the moment of inertia $I$ and lowering rotational energy by the quartic centrifugal distortion term $-D J^2(J+1)^2$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a non-equivalent two-electron configuration $2p 3p$ in $LS$ coupling. How many distinct $^{2S+1}L$ terms (ignoring $J$ splitting) are possible?
questions.explanationEn: Since the electrons are non-equivalent, Pauli exclusion does not restrict combinations: $L \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ ($S, P, D$) and $S \in \{0, 1\}$ (singlet, triplet), giving $3 \times 2 = 6$ terms: $^1 S, ^3 S, ^1 P, ^3 P, ^1 D, ^3 D$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In the anomalous Zeeman effect for the sodium $D_2$ transition ($^2 P_{3/2} \to {}^2 S_{1/2}$), how many distinct Zeeman components appear in a weak magnetic field?
questions.explanationEn: $^2 P_{3/2}$ has 4 sublevels ($M_J = \pm 3/2, \pm 1/2$, $g = 4/3$) and $^2 S_{1/2}$ has 2 sublevels ($M_J = \pm 1/2$, $g = 2$). Allowed $\Delta M_J = 0, \pm 1$ transitions: 2 with $\Delta M_J = 0$ and 4 with $\Delta M_J = \pm 1$, giving 6 distinct lines.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about X-ray spectra produced by bombarding a metal target with high-energy electrons are TRUE?
optionsEn: The continuous Bremsstrahlung spectrum has a sharp short-wavelength cutoff $\lambda_{\min} = hc/(eV)$ that depends ONLY on the accelerating voltage $V$, not on the target material
$K_\beta$ photons have higher energy (shorter wavelength) than $K_\alpha$ photons for the same target
Increasing the tube current (at fixed voltage $V$) decreases $\lambda_{\min}$
Characteristic $K_\alpha$ and $K_\beta$ lines depend on the atomic number $Z$ of the target element
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are exact ($K_\beta$ is $M \to K$, higher energy than $K_\alpha$ which is $L \to K$). Increasing tube current increases intensity but leaves $\lambda_{\min} = hc/(eV)$ unchanged (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: The $v = 0 \to 1$ fundamental vibrational transition of a diatomic molecule occurs at $2900\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and the $v = 0 \to 2$ first overtone occurs at $5700\text{ cm}^{-1}$. What is the equilibrium harmonic frequency $\bar{\nu}_e$ (in $\text{cm}^{-1}$)?

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In a rovibrational spectrum of HCl, the $R(0)$ line is at $2906\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and the $P(1)$ line is at $2866\text{ cm}^{-1}$. What is the rotational constant $B$ (in $\text{cm}^{-1}$)?

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the spin multiplicity ($2S + 1$) of the ground state of a fluorine atom ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^5$)?
questions.explanationEn: $2p^5$ has 1 unpaired electron (1 hole), so $S = 1/2$ and multiplicity $2S + 1 = 2$ ($^2 P_{3/2}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In a diatomic molecule, the pure rotational line $J = 0 \to 1$ has wavenumber $10\text{ cm}^{-1}$. What is the rotational energy of the $J = 3$ level (in $\text{cm}^{-1}$)?
questions.explanationEn: $2B = 10 \implies B = 5\text{ cm}^{-1}$. Rotational energy $E_3 = B J(J+1) = 5(3)(4) = 60\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In a $^3 P$ multiplet obeying the Landé interval rule, the separation between $^3 P_2$ and $^3 P_1$ is $40\text{ cm}^{-1}$. What is the separation between $^3 P_1$ and $^3 P_0$ (in $\text{cm}^{-1}$)?
questions.explanationEn: $E(J) - E(J-1) = A J$, so $E(2) - E(1) = 2A = 40 \implies A = 20\text{ cm}^{-1}$. Thus $E(1) - E(0) = 1 \cdot A = 20\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: For an ESR experiment on a free radical ($g = 2.0$) at microwave frequency $\nu = 9.5\text{ GHz}$, taking $\mu_B / h = 14.0\text{ GHz/T}$, what magnetic field $B_0$ (in Tesla, rounded to 3 decimal places) is required for resonance?
questions.explanationEn: $h\nu = g \mu_B B_0 \implies B_0 = \frac{\nu}{g (\mu_B / h)} = \frac{9.5}{2.0 \times 14.0} = \frac{9.5}{28.0} \approx 0.339\text{ T}$.
